summary: Robbins Hill tower in Chelmsford, MA: fire lookout since 1911 (state-bought summit from 1918); the 68-foot tower dates from 1939, after the 1938 hurricane. Today's staffing and access are undocumented.

facts.design: 68-foot tower with a 10 by 10 foot cab (steel tower per the Forest Lookouts page)
facts.agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control

events.note: First tower on the summit: 30 feet high, reached by a ladder (Parkhurst column)
Second tower, 75 feet per the state forester report quoted on Forest Lookouts; the column says 68 feet
Destroyed in the Great New England Hurricane, September 21, 1938
68-foot steel tower with 10 by 10 foot cab, replacing the one lost in 1938; the Register description says constructed 1938

Several of the most experienced tower operators, including the town's own local operator, were now on new work; the same section says the new rearmament program was already causing an extreme shortage of help at fires
Forest warden's report: 124 actual fires in the year and over 20 investigations of calls made from the tower
Wooden cab completely replaced, about 1970 (Parkhurst column)
Column written about 1986 names a present observer; the observer said the tower serves only to elevate someone else's antennae, which have nothing to do with the forest fire service
Registered May 14, 2008 as US 732, MA 43; nominated by Henry Isenberg
State forest fire control maintenance crew repaired minor vandalism damage

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register's Built field and the Forest Lookouts page give 1939, and the column says the tower went up the summer after the 1938 storm. The Register description says constructed 1938. 1939 is kept as the build year; the 1938 date is noted.

The 1918 tower is 75 feet in the state forester report quoted on Forest Lookouts and 68 feet in the Parkhurst column. The present tower is 68 feet in all three sources, so the present tower's height is not in dispute.

notes_for_editor: Today's status, staffing, access and rental are unverified. No source read is later than the 2019 blog post, and the record's access 'unknown' is kept (no access facts added). Name variants: Robbins Hill (NHLR and Forest Lookouts text), Robbin Hill (Forest Lookouts title), Robin's Hill (column). Conflicts: (a) build year, NHLR description says 1938 while its Built field and the Forest Lookouts page say 1939; 1939 kept. (b) 1918 tower height, 75 ft (state forester report quoted on Forest Lookouts) vs 68 ft (column). (c) Count: NHLR and column call the present tower the fourth on the site, but the accounts read name only three towers (1911, 1918, 1939); the missing one is unidentified. (d) Cab: NHLR gives a wooden cab and the column says the wooden cab was replaced about 1970; the Forest Lookouts page calls the tower steel. Not used: a search snippet of an FFLA Massachusetts Facebook post and a Summit House blog post give a 38-foot 1911 tower and a 1945 road to the lookout; these pages were not read in full, so they are leads only. Also unread: chelmhist.org Summit House blog and the Chelmsford fire department history 1822-1994 PDF, which mentions a proposed state tower on Robbins Hill. Ownership: the column does not say who held the 1911 tower, so the story does not say the state held it in 1911; the 1918 state report says the state had maintained a tower there for six years. The column is an OCR scan; quotes were taken from the cached text. The 'as_of 1986' staffing date is the column's date. No photos added: the 1940-1949 history page has a reconstruction caption (credited to the Chelmsford Historical Society Collection) but no image URL was found.
